overview.text: Central Bank of India seeks share broking houses to offer an online share trading platform and Demat support services to its customers under its 3-in-1 scheme (savings account, Demat account, trading account). Contract is 3 years from go-live, extendable. There should be no cost to the Bank; bidders quote a revenue share.

summary.issuing_organization: Central Bank of India; Resources Department, 4th Floor, Chander Mukhi, Nariman Point, Mumbai-400001; RFP Ref No. GEM/2025/B/6828132 dated 27/10/2025; bids to Deputy General Manager, Resources Department, 1st Floor, Bajaj Bhavan, Nariman Point, Mumbai 400021; Tel 022-66387502/7780

scope.text: Open the customer's Demat account with the Bank and trading account with the broker in one seamless digital journey on the Bank's CenteeZ app and other digital channels; preferable turnaround is 10-15 minutes.

Provide a web and mobile online trading platform with real-time market data, market, limit and stop-loss orders, call and trade, reports, and trading in NSE and BSE secondary market, IPO, Govt securities, mutual funds, futures and options, sovereign gold bonds, currency, REITs and fixed income.

Integrate the platform with the Bank's core banking, DPSecure back office and CDSL/NSDL systems, with fund transfer and lien marking and unmarking on Demat holdings; back-office integration is at the bidder's cost.
Provide Demat support services: grievance redressal, control register, register of investor customers, MIS reports, and a dedicated website with complaint tracking including SEBI SCORES.
Promote the 3-in-1 scheme across the country and train Bank staff at Central Office, Zonal Offices, Regional Offices and branches; give on-site handholding to corporate customers who opt in.
Award is not exclusive: the Bank already has a tie-up with Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd (MOFSL) and plans one or more additional partners.
Platform should also support loan against shares, BTST, algorithmic trading and a pre-built basket of stocks and ETFs; Margin Trading Facility (MTF) may be provided, with risks borne by the bidder.
Provide reverse transition and seamless migration to the Bank or a new bidder on exit, including training and documentation; its cost must be part of the commercial offer.

key_requirements.text: Bidder must comply with all points mentioned in the Scope of work, although many are worded 'should'; non-compliance of any point will lead to rejection of the bid.
Technical and functional requirements in Annexure IX must be 100% complied with; any non-compliance may lead to disqualification.
Bidder must have a trading platform approved by CDSL and NSDL, be versed with CDSL's CDAS and the NSDL Demat system, and settle transactions in e-mode.
Bidder must implement STP to insert transactions into the Bank's DPSecure back office, CDSL's CDAS or the NSDL Demat application, and integrate with the Bank's TCS Bancs-24 core banking system.
Platform must be hosted at the bidder's premises in High Availability mode with minimum uptime of 99.95 %, support DC/DR architecture, and be supported 24*7*365.

Platform must support authentication through tokens or soft token, OTP, digital certificates, IP address and mobile application, and record user ID, IP address and Mac address of each transaction for audit.
Regulatory changes by SEBI, RBI or the depositories must be implemented immediately within prescribed times at free of cost to the Bank.
Bidder must promptly rectify all discrepancies observed in security audits at no additional cost to the Bank.
If the Bank's core banking system is upgraded or replaced, the bidder must keep the integration working without any additional cost.
Trading services must be provided only to customers who compulsorily avail Demat services of Central Bank of India.

eligibility.text: Bidder must be a legal entity in India, preferably a Public/Private limited company majority owned by Indian residents; Government organisations, PSE/PSU and start-ups meeting all other criteria are also eligible.
Bidder must be in broking business with valid SEBI registration and valid NSE and BSE membership, and have minimum 5 years of experience in broking business operations.

Bidder must have positive net worth and positive net profit in the last three financial years (FY 2022-23, FY 23-24 & FY 24-25), shown by audited statements and a Chartered Accountant net worth certificate; provisional statements certified by a Chartered Accountant are accepted for FY 24-25 if audited results are unavailable.
Bidder must have Pan India experience with retail clients and be tied up with at least one scheduled commercial bank for trading services; this does not apply to Government/PSE/PSU bidders.

Bidder must not be an associate or subsidiary of a banking company or vice versa, and must be non-bank promoted: not promoted by competitor banks or their controlling groups, and no competitor bank holding equity of 10% and above or having a Board representative.

There must be no suspension order against the bidder by SEBI, NSDL, CDSL, NSE or BSE in the past three years, and no restraint order pending at any judicial forum in India or abroad on broking business.
Bidder must have a trading platform approved by NSDL and CDSL with all transactions settled in e-mode, supported by an undertaking.
A bidder from a country sharing a land border with India is eligible only if registered with the Competent Authority.

The Bank may offer an incentive on a per account basis for converted leads; the amount is not stated.

project_duration.text: Contract period is 3 years from the date of successful go live or acceptance by the Bank; the Bank may renew for a further 3 years and keep renewing on mutually acceptable terms.

Annexure VIII stages: project plan within 1 weeks, implementation within 2 weeks, User Acceptance and Audit Closure within 3 weeks, UAT and go-live within 5 weeks of purchase order acceptance.
The selected bidder must execute the SLA within 45 days from acceptance of the Purchase Order/Letter of Intent.
The Bank may cancel if the bidder fails to accept the contract within 30 days of receipt of the purchase order.
Reverse transition runs for a period of 6 months after the 90-day notice period, and is activated on cancellation or 6 months before expiry of the contract.

important_conditions.text: Evaluation: Three stages - eligibility cum technical bid, technical evaluation, commercial bid evaluation; a cut-off score of 70% in technical evaluation is needed to qualify for commercial bid opening.

Evaluation: Technical marks total 150: experience 50 (10 per public sector bank implementation up to 30, 4 per private bank up to 20), five parameters at 5 each (branches, Banca Demat accounts, tie-up period, manpower, online turnover), product functionality 25 (Annexure IX: 1 mark available, 0 not), presentation or demo 50.
Evaluation: Final selection is on highest commercial; the bidder sharing the highest percentage of net revenue is H-1 and is selected; a tie goes to the highest technical score.

Submission: Bids go only through the GeM portal (fax or mail are rejected) as Technical Bid Part I and Commercial Bid Part II, submitted separately; price information in the technical bid may lead to rejection.

Submission: Hard copies of the Integrity Pact and Non Disclosure Agreement, in an envelope superscripted as the RFP, must reach the Deputy General Manager, Resources Department, Bajaj Bhavan by 3.00 PM on 20/11/2025.

Submission: Offers without a signed Integrity Pact along with the technical bid are summarily rejected; all pages of the Integrity Pact must be signed and stamped, and each page of the bid signed and stamped by the authorised person.

Submission: Required forms include Annexure I application, Annexure II bidder information, Annexure X undertaking on non-judicial stamp paper and Annexure XI non-blacklisting undertaking, which also says no legal action is pending for any cause.
Submission: Risk management measures are to be submitted along with the technical bid.

Risk: Indemnity is subject to a limit agreed between the parties under the RFP, but no limit is stated; indemnity also covers claims by customers and regulatory authorities.
Risk: The Bank may terminate at any time on Thirty (30) days written notice without assigning any reason, with no termination compensation payable to the bidder.

overview.text: IIM Tiruchirappalli invites sealed proposals (RFP No. 24SPT291T dated 08.01.2025) to select a branding agency. The agency will define the brand purpose, revisit the logo for the digital era, and produce a comprehensive branding guidelines document with designs, artworks and an implementation plan, across English, Hindi and Tamil and sub-brands. Part A is estimated at Rs. 11,00,000/- excluding GST, to be completed within 90 days of the Work Order.

summary.issuing_organization: Indian Institute of Management Tiruchirappalli (IIM Tiruchirappalli), Ministry of Education, Government of India; RFP No. 24SPT291T dated 08.01.2025; Chief Administrative Officer (i/c), Trichy - Pudukkottai Main Road, Tiruchirappalli-620 024; purchase@iimtrichy.ac.in

scope.text: Define the brand purpose: stakeholder discussions, competitor and industry analysis, feedback from students, faculty and alumni, articulation of purpose, mission, vision and values, and target-audience personas.
Revisit the logo for the digital era: contemporary design appealing to millennial and GenZ audiences, versatile across digital platforms in colour and monochrome, keeping the original logo's essence.

Comprehensive branding guidelines document and digital Brand Identity Manual: colour palette, typography, iconography, imagery, logo usage rules, graphic elements, and do's and don'ts, covering sub-brands such as Chennai Campus, Placements and EEC.

Signage designs and artworks for Trichy Campus and Chennai Campus in bilingual (Hindi, English) and trilingual (Tamil, Hindi, English) versions, for classrooms, offices, auditorium, entrances, sports block and other locations.

Stationery designs for Trichy Campus and Chennai Centre: business cards, identity cards, letterheads (A4, A5, Legal), note sheets, envelopes, visitor passes, corporate gift boxes and memento packaging.

Advertising and promotion templates: print, TV logo closure, BTL, OOH and event materials, social media graphics and post templates, an IIM Tiruchirappalli hashtag, merchandise, brochures and video guidelines.
Web page guidelines for the Institute's website: layout, font sizes, line heights, spacing, colour usage, accessibility, cross-device performance and standards for images, icons and multimedia.
Implementation plan for introducing the new brand identity internally and externally, which may include training stakeholders on brand usage.

key_requirements.text: The bidder must not sub-let or subcontract any part of the contract to another agency or individual.

Branding guidelines must specify preferred materials/make and suitable substitutes for applications such as sign boards, office interiors, furniture, painting, wallpapers, vinyl, printing and paper type.
A well-defined colour palette must be developed; it should adhere to web accessibility standards and guide colour combinations in different contexts.

Before starting branding work, the successful bidder should answer the prerequisite brand questions (journey in less than 500 words, 3 key messages, strengths, benefits, desired perception) with IIM stakeholders.
As the first stage, the bidder is required to conduct a study with IIM Tiruchirappalli to finalize requirements and submit a phased work plan and delivery schedule for approval.
The Brand Identity guidelines deliverables should be crafted as interactive web pages hosted on the Institute's official website.
The successful bidder will be required to collaborate with the separately contracted website development and branding teams so the website aligns with the approved branding.

The bidder must warrant that deliverables do not infringe third-party trademark, copyright, patent or trade secret rights, obtain licences where needed, and indemnify IIM Tiruchirappalli against infringement liability.
IIM Tiruchirappalli will own the rights to the branding work on completion, with full rights to use, modify and distribute the materials without limitation.
The vendor should protect the Institute's proprietary and confidential information; failure will lead to legal action.

eligibility.text: Must be registered for GST; GST registration certificate, PAN and bank account details must be submitted with the Technical Bid, with names matching the RFP document.
Must be registered with the appropriate authority and in operation for at least five years as of December 31, 2024; Certificate of Incorporation or registration required.

Must have at least five years of experience in similar work as of December 31, 2024, i.e. branding for large businesses, MNCs, reputed private organizations, Government of India organizations, banks, NIRF 2024 top-50 academic institutions or state governments.
Digital or social media marketing does not count as branding; work done through subcontractors or for the bidder's own or sister companies is not accepted.

Similar projects in the past five years: one costing 80% or more, two costing 60% or more, or three costing 40% or more of the estimated tender cost; work orders executed between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2024.
Average annual turnover for 2021-22 to 2023-24 must be at least 100% of the estimated tender cost; audited balance sheets with profit and loss statements must be submitted.
Must be regular in filing Income Tax returns; returns and audited accounts for 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24 to be submitted with the Technical Bid.
Must not be blacklisted by any Government of India department, State Government or private organization, with no criminal case against the firm or its owners/partners; undertaking per Annexure - III.
